claims.assertion: This was a metered RydeTAXI trip, so the fare is built from distance and time units and any unexcused extra kilometres were billed to the rider.
The trip ran 9.3 km against a 3.9 km optimal route (+5.4 km, +136%), and the two off-route segments added 1.63 km (F4) and 2.83 km (F5) respectively.

The rider's own message consented only to 'go round by Cavenagh' (F10-F11), so that consent covers only the Cavenagh diversion, not the later 3.60 km segment out to Beach Road, which was never put to the rider before it was taken.

Even for the Cavenagh segment, the driver's own pre-trip message (F10) and the driver's post-trip statement (F14) are unsupported by the traffic record: the only LTA incident, an accident at 13:52 on Orchard Road, sits 30 m from the optimal route and was cleared before the driver's own proposed Cavenagh detour, while Orchard Road band 1 (0-9 km/h) covers only 14:00-14:10.

The 4 min 10 s stop at (1.3025, 103.8638), 2995 m from the pickup and 2098 m from the drop-off, lies inside the 3.60 km off-route segment, matching the driver's admission in F14 that he chose a 7-Eleven he knows on Beach Road; the rider named no place and was not told which one, so that segment's extra kilometres are not excused by the stop request.

Billed excess distance is $7.58 at $1.41/km, so the rider's refund is the sum of the unexcused segments' extra km: 1.63 km (F4) plus 2.83 km (F5) = 4.46 km x $1.41/km = $6.29 (only 0.25 km of the 5.4 km billed excess is left as mapping residual).

The driver charged $1.08 of waiting time (4.2 min) on this RydeTAXI trip; the waiting units attach to the 7-Eleven stop the driver selected unannounced (F2/F14), so the rider should at least have the discretionary element of that charge reviewed with the route refund.
The driver has 3 disputes with 1 upheld in 90 days, but no upheld route dispute, so the account-review add-on threshold in RD-6 is not met on this record.

weaknesses: The rider really did send 'Sure. Can you stop at a 7-Eleven on the way?' (F11) at 14:02, before the first off-route segment started at 14:10 (F4); the driver will argue this is advance consent to the whole routing, and RD-3(a) can excuse a stop the rider requested.
The rider agreed to the Cavenagh diversion (F10-F11), so the driver will say segment F4 (1.63 km, 14:10-14:13) is an agreed route change under RD-5 and only F5 is in play.

The driver's statement (F14) claims a jam caused by an accident and that the rider agreed; the 13:52 accident at 30 m from the optimal route and Orchard Road band 1 for 14:00-14:10 (F15, F18) give the driver partial support for the early diversion even though he has no incident evidence for the 14:17-14:29 segment.

The rider has not shown the Beach Road 7-Eleven was chosen without notice other than the driver's own statement and the short gap between F11 and F12; the driver may argue 'the 7-Eleven on the way' was understood as a specific store.
The $6.29 figure rests on the segment sums (F4+F5 = 4.46 km) rather than the billed 5.4 km excess (F1/F6), so the judge may either trim it further or add the 0.25 km residual back.

claims.assertion: Segment 1 (14:10–14:13, +1.63 km) is exempt under RD-4(a): an LTA DataMall accident on Orchard Road towards Bras Basah after Cavenagh Road, two lanes closed, was reported at 13:52 and sits 30 m from the optimal route, so it is on the replaced stretch of the optimal route and predates the segment, which falls inside the trip window.

The severe-congestion record on the replaced optimal route corroborates the reroute: Orchard Road shows speed band 1 (0–9 km/h) during 14:00–14:10, immediately before and at the start of segment 1 (14:10), i.e. the driver was leaving a road that was effectively stationary.

The rider consented in advance to the Cavenagh reroute: at 14:01 the driver asked 'ok if I go round by Cavenagh?' and at 14:02 the rider replied 'Sure. Can you stop at a 7-Eleven on the way?' — the 'Sure' is the rider's own message, sent before segment 1 started at 14:10, and the rider's only additional request was a stop, not a change of route.

The rider named the shop type ('a 7-Eleven on the way') but not a location, so under RD-3(b) the diversion created by the stop is not automatically exempt: the Beach Road 7-Eleven detour should be treated as an unexempted segment, which is why the driver only asks for partial relief rather than a full defence.

The stop itself was a genuine 4 min 10 s stationary period at 14:20–14:24, at a point that is neither pickup nor drop-off (2995 m from pickup, 2098 m from drop-off) — consistent with the driver's account of stopping at a 7-Eleven, not with a joyride or an unexplained halt.

The residual excess after exempting segment 1 and the stop segment is small relative to the complaint: total excess distance billed is $7.58 (5.4 km × $1.41/km) on a $25.40 RydeTAXI metered fare, and segments 1 and 2 together account for 4.46 km of the 5.4 km, so any refund must be limited to the unpaid-for part of segment 2, not the whole excess.

No account flag is warranted against the driver under RD-6: the profile shows only 1 upheld dispute in 90 days and it is a no-show dispute, with route disputes upheld in the last 90 days at 0, so this case would not make him 'repeated' for routing.

The waiting charge of $1.08 is a metered RydeTAXI waiting unit (4.2 min × $0.26/min) matching the 4 min 10 s stationary stop, and under RD-3(c) metered waiting time on a RydeTAXI trip is chargeable and is not refunded.
